examples.ko: 우리 부모님은 안정적인 우량주에만 오래 투자하세요.
examples.en: My parents only invest in stable blue-chip stocks for the long term.
This company is counted as a typical blue chip.

examples.ko: 주식을 처음 사는 사람은 우량주부터 공부해 보세요.
examples.en: If you are buying stocks for the first time, start by studying blue chips.
Even blue-chip stocks drop in price sometimes.

examples.ko: 요즘 우량주 중심으로 포트폴리오를 바꾸고 있어요.
examples.en: These days I am changing my portfolio to center on blue chips.

examples.ko: 배당을 잘 주는 우량주를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for blue-chip stocks that pay good dividends.

explain: '대형주'는 회사 규모를 기준으로 하고, '우량주'는 실적과 재무 상태가 탄탄해서 안정적이라고 보는 주식을 말할 때 써요. '블루칩'이라고도 해요. 뉴스나 투자 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '대형주' (large-cap stock) is based on company size, while '우량주' is used for stocks seen as stable because of solid earnings and finances. People also say '블루칩'. It often appears in news and investment talk.

examples.en: It was an apology from the heart, so my anger melted.
This tea is good to drink once it has steeped for about three minutes.

examples.ko: 멸치를 오래 끓였더니 국물이 진하게 우러나왔어요.
examples.en: I boiled the anchovies for a long time, and the broth came out rich.

examples.ko: 마음에서 우러나오는 감사 인사를 전하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to give thanks that come from my heart.

examples.ko: 억지로 하지 말고 마음이 우러나올 때 도와주세요.
examples.en: Don't force it; help when you feel like it from the heart.

examples.ko: 사골은 오래 끓여야 맛이 제대로 우러나와요.
examples.en: Beef bone broth needs long boiling for the flavor to come out properly.

explain: '진심에서 우러나오다'처럼 억지가 아니라 저절로 생기는 마음에 자주 써요. 국물이나 차에서는 재료를 오래 끓이거나 담글 때 맛이 배어 나오는 걸 말하고, '우러나다'도 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is often used in '진심에서 우러나오다' for feelings that arise naturally, not by force. For broth or tea it describes flavor seeping out after long boiling or steeping, and '우러나다' is used the same way.

examples.ko: 아이는 높은 산을 우러러 한참 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The child stood for a long time looking up at the high mountain.

examples.ko: 저는 평생 교육에 힘쓴 할머니를 우러르며 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to live looking up to my grandmother, who devoted her life to education.
If you look up at the sky, you can see it full of stars.
People respect and look up to that doctor.

examples.ko: 고개를 들어 높은 탑을 우러르고 있어요.
examples.en: I am raising my head and looking up at the tall tower.
He is an elder whom everyone looks up to.

explain: '우러러요', '우러러'처럼 활용해요. 하늘이나 높은 곳을 올려다볼 때와 사람을 높이 존경할 때, 두 가지로 써요. 글이나 연설 같은 격식 있는 느낌이라, 말할 때는 '우러러보다'나 '존경하다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It conjugates as '우러러요' and '우러러'. It is used both for looking up at the sky or a high place and for deeply respecting a person. It sounds formal or literary, so in speech people more often say '우러러보다' or '존경하다'.

examples.en: Thunder rumbled in the distance.
The sky rumbled, and then the rain poured down.

examples.ko: 밤새 우르릉 소리가 들려서 잠을 설쳤어요.
examples.en: I heard a rumbling sound all night and slept badly.

examples.ko: 우르릉 쾅 하는 소리에 아이가 놀라서 울었어요.
examples.en: The child was startled by the rumble and bang and cried.

examples.ko: 산 너머에서 우르릉 소리가 점점 가까워져요.
examples.en: The rumbling from beyond the mountain is getting closer.

examples.ko: 기차가 우르릉 하고 다리 위를 지나갔어요.
examples.en: The train rumbled across the bridge.

explain: 천둥이나 큰 기계, 기차가 내는 낮고 무거운 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. '우르릉 쾅쾅'처럼 '쾅'과 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It imitates the low, heavy sound of thunder, big machines or trains. It is often paired with '쾅' as in '우르릉 쾅쾅'.

examples.en: Thunder is rumbling among the dark clouds.
The sky rumbled, and soon a shower fell.
The machines at the construction site rumbled all day.

examples.ko: 멀리서 우르릉거리는 소리가 들려서 창문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: I heard a rumbling sound far away, so I closed the window.
It looks like thunder will rumble from the evening.
A truck rumbled through the alley.

explain: 주로 천둥, 큰 차, 기계 소리에 써요. 사람 배에서 나는 소리는 '꾸르륵'이라고 해요. '우르릉대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for thunder, big vehicles and machines. A rumbling stomach is '꾸르륵' instead. '우르릉대다' is used with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 귀가 있어도 듣지 못하는 우매한 사람들과 무슨 얘기를 하겠어요?
examples.en: What is there to talk about with foolish people who have ears but cannot hear?

examples.ko: 저는 우매해서 그때는 그 말의 뜻을 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was foolish, so I did not understand what those words meant back then.

examples.ko: 그런 결정을 내리다니 제가 너무 우매했어요.
examples.en: I was so foolish to make that kind of decision.

examples.ko: 우매하다고 비웃기 전에 먼저 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Before you laugh at them as ignorant, please explain first.
He is someone who regards the public as ignorant.

examples.ko: 우매할수록 남의 말을 더 쉽게 믿어요.
examples.en: The more ignorant a person is, the more easily they believe others.

explain: '어리석다'보다 딱딱한 글말이라 연설, 글, 역사 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '어리석다'나 '멍청하다'를 쓰는데, 남에게 '우매하다'고 하면 매우 무례하게 들려요.
explain_en: It is a stiffer, written word than '어리석다', common in speeches, essays and history. In daily talk people say '어리석다' or '멍청하다', and calling someone '우매하다' sounds very rude.

examples.ko: 땅이 우묵해서 비가 오면 물이 고여요.
examples.en: The ground is hollowed, so water collects when it rains.
Please put the soup in a deep, hollow bowl.
Your eyes look sunken, so you seem tired.
The spot where the ball fell has become dented.
The middle of the road is dipped, so be careful.

examples.ko: 우묵하다고 해서 다 깊은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because it is hollowed doesn't mean it is deep.

explain: 가운데가 안쪽으로 둥글게 들어간 모양에 써요. 일상 말로는 '움푹하다'나 '움푹 패다'를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요. 눈이 들어가 피곤해 보일 때는 '눈이 퀭하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a shape whose middle sinks inward in a rounded way. In everyday speech you may hear '움푹하다' or '움푹 패다' more often. For sunken, tired-looking eyes people also say '눈이 퀭하다'.

en: wise answer to a stupid question

examples.en: The question was off the wall, but the answer was great, so it was a wise answer to a silly question.

examples.ko: 선생님의 우문현답 덕분에 제 고민이 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my teacher's wise answer to my silly question, my worry was solved.
A wise reply to a silly question came up in the interview, and everyone laughed.
This is exactly what we call a wise answer to a silly question.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 우문현답은 인터넷에서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That singer's clever answer to a silly question became a hot topic online.

examples.ko: 기자가 이상한 질문을 하자 감독이 우문현답으로 받아쳤어요.
examples.en: When the reporter asked a strange question, the coach shot back with a clever answer.

explain: 인터뷰나 방송에서 엉뚱한 질문에 재치 있는 대답이 나왔을 때 칭찬처럼 써요. 자기 질문을 낮춰 '우문에 현답'이라고 띄어서 말하기도 해요. 질문한 사람을 은근히 낮추는 말이 될 수 있으니 상대의 질문에는 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It is used like praise when a clever answer comes to an odd question, often in interviews or on TV. People also say '우문에 현답' with a space, putting down their own question. It can subtly belittle the asker, so be careful using it about someone else's question.

examples.en: The child is chewing slowly with food in the mouth.
Grandmother eats her rice slowly, chewing it over.

examples.ko: 그는 대답을 못 하고 우물거리기만 했어요.
examples.en: He couldn't answer and only mumbled.
Don't mumble; try speaking up.
I mumbled in the interview and couldn't finish what I wanted to say.
He mumbled something, but I couldn't make out a word.

explain: 입 안에서 음식을 씹는 모양과 말을 분명하지 않게 하는 모양, 두 가지로 써요. 말하는 쪽은 '웅얼거리다'나 '얼버무리다'와 비슷한데, '얼버무리다'는 일부러 분명하게 말하지 않는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used both for chewing slowly in the mouth and for speaking unclearly. For speech it is close to '웅얼거리다' and '얼버무리다', and '얼버무리다' has a feel of deliberately not being clear.

examples.ko: 아이가 빵을 입에 가득 넣고 우물우물 씹어요.
examples.en: The child chews bread slowly with a full mouth.

examples.ko: 그는 말해 놓고 우물우물 김치를 씹었어요.
examples.en: After saying it, he slowly chewed his kimchi.
Don't mumble your answer; say it clearly.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 우물우물 무슨 말씀을 하셨는데 잘 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: Grandfather mumbled something, but I couldn't hear it well.

examples.ko: 학생이 우물우물 변명을 늘어놓자 선생님이 한숨을 쉬셨어요.
examples.en: When the student mumbled out excuses, the teacher sighed.

examples.ko: 강아지가 간식을 우물우물 먹다가 나를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The puppy chewed its treat and then looked at me.

explain: 입 안에서 천천히 씹는 모양과 말을 흐리는 모양, 두 가지에 써요. 단단한 것을 거칠게 씹는 '우적우적'과는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used for both slow chewing in the mouth and unclear mumbling. It feels different from '우적우적', which is for crunching hard food roughly.

examples.en: The United States is a longtime ally of our country.
The two countries regard each other as friendly nations.
Representatives of allied countries gathered in Seoul.
They decided to solve the problem in cooperation with allied nations.

examples.ko: 위기가 오면 우방국의 도움이 정말 중요해요.
examples.en: When a crisis comes, help from allies is really important.
The president plans to visit friendly nations one by one.

explain: 뉴스나 외교 이야기에서 나오는 말이에요. 사이가 좋은 나라를 가리키고, 군사 동맹까지 맺은 나라는 '동맹국'이라고 해서 둘이 늘 같지는 않아요. 반대로 사이가 나쁜 나라는 '적대국'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It appears in news and diplomacy talk for countries on good terms. A country with a military alliance is called '동맹국', so the two words are not always the same. Hostile countries are called '적대국'.

examples.en: Excessive idolization of celebrities is dangerous.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 지도자의 우상화를 강요한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that country forces the idolization of its leader.
When idolization gets worse, it becomes hard to criticize.

examples.ko: 역사 속 인물을 우상화 없이 객관적으로 배우고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to learn about historical figures objectively, without idolizing them.

examples.ko: 스타의 우상화 현상이 사회 문제로 이야기되고 있어요.
examples.en: The phenomenon of idolizing stars is being discussed as a social problem.

examples.ko: 팬들의 우상화에 선수도 부담을 느낀다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The player said he also feels pressure from the fans' idolization.

explain: 사람을 신처럼 떠받드는 일이라 대부분 비판하는 뉘앙스로 써요. 비슷한 말로 '신격화'가 있어요. 칭찬하는 '존경'과는 달리, 잘못도 못 보게 만든다는 느낌이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It means treating a person like a god, so it usually carries a critical tone. A similar word is '신격화'. Unlike respectful '존경', it implies that people can no longer see the person's faults.

examples.en: The media idolizes that player too much.

examples.ko: 사람을 우상화하면 잘못도 못 보게 돼요.
examples.en: If you idolize someone, you can't even see their faults.

examples.ko: 가수는 팬들이 자기를 우상화하지 않았으면 좋겠다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The singer said he hoped fans wouldn't idolize him.
I am worried that more people are idolizing politicians.
When I was little, I idolized my father.

examples.ko: 영웅을 우상화해서 가르치면 안 된다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think we shouldn't teach about heroes by idolizing them.

explain: '을/를'과 함께 써서 '누구를 우상화하다'라고 말해요. 단순히 좋아하는 것이 아니라 완벽한 사람처럼 떠받든다는 비판적인 느낌이 있어요. 반대 느낌으로는 '깎아내리다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It takes '을/를' as in '누구를 우상화하다'. It is not just liking someone; it has a critical sense of putting them on a pedestal as perfect. The opposite feel is '깎아내리다' (to run down).

examples.ko: 서류를 우송하는 데 보통 이삼 일이 걸려서 일정에 여유를 두었어요.
examples.en: Mailing documents usually takes two or three days, so I left some leeway in the schedule.
I'll mail the contract to your address tomorrow.

examples.ko: 책을 우송하려면 먼저 포장부터 해야 해요.
examples.en: To mail the book, you need to wrap it first.

examples.ko: 합격 증서를 집으로 우송했다고 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: I got word that they mailed the certificate of acceptance to my home.
I received the documents you mailed today.
I'll mail the item this afternoon.

explain: 우편으로 보낸다는 점이 분명한 딱딱한 말이라 공문이나 안내문에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '부치다'나 '보내다'를 쓰고, 택배로 보낼 때는 '택배로 보내다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal word that makes clear something goes by post, so it appears in official notices. In daily life people say '부치다' or '보내다', and for courier delivery '택배로 보내다'.

examples.ko: 바람이 불자 낙엽이 우수수 떨어져서 길이 노랗게 변했어요.
examples.en: When the wind blew, leaves fell in a flurry and the road turned yellow.
When I shook the tree, chestnuts rained down.
In autumn, ginkgo leaves come fluttering down.

examples.ko: 책장에서 책이 우수수 쏟아져서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Books tumbled out of the bookshelf, and I was startled.
Snow fell from the roof in clumps.
Coins spilled out of my pocket.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 여러 개 한꺼번에 떨어지는 모양에 써요. 낙엽, 열매, 동전처럼 많이 떨어지는 것에 잘 어울려요. 건물이 크게 무너지는 모양은 '와르르'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes many small, light things falling all at once, which suits fallen leaves, nuts or coins. A big collapse is described with '와르르' instead.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 우승권에 들어갈 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can our team get into title contention?
At the current standings, the title looks out of reach.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 우승권 밖에서 출발했지만 끝까지 달렸어요.
examples.en: The runner started outside the winning group but ran to the end.

examples.ko: 우승권을 노리는 팀이 세 팀이나 돼요.
examples.en: Three teams are aiming for the title.

examples.ko: 우승권과 거리가 먼 팀이라서 부담이 없어요.
examples.en: We are far from title contention, so there is no pressure.
After winning in a row late in the season, they climbed into title contention.

explain: '우승권에 들다', '우승권에 있다'처럼 쓰고 스포츠 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 같은 식으로 '상위권', '중위권', '하위권'이라는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '우승권에 들다' and '우승권에 있다', and often appears in sports news. There are parallel words such as '상위권', '중위권' and '하위권'.

examples.ko: 그 남자는 우악스럽게 문을 밀고 들어왔어요.
examples.en: The man pushed the door roughly and came in.
His hands look rough, but his heart is warm.
The child was startled by the harsh voice.

examples.ko: 겉모습은 우악스럽지 않지만 힘이 정말 세요.
examples.en: He doesn't look rough, but he is really strong.
Contrary to the rumor that he was rough, the man was kind.
His rough first impression has softened a lot now.

explain: 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '우악스러워요'로 바뀌어요. 말투나 행동, 손힘이 거칠고 억세 보일 때 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '거칠다', '억세다'가 있어요. 대체로 좋은 뜻은 아니에요.
explain_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '우악스러워요'. It is used when speech, behavior or hand strength looks rough and forceful, similar to '거칠다' and '억세다'. It is usually not a compliment.

examples.ko: 오늘 우리 팀 선발 투수는 우완이에요.
examples.en: Our team's starting pitcher today is a right-hander.

examples.ko: 새로 온 우완 투수가 공이 정말 빨라요.
examples.en: The new right-handed pitcher throws really fast.
It is a team with more right-handers than left-handers.
That player is called the right-handed ace.

examples.ko: 그 투수는 우완이지만 왼손으로도 글씨를 써요.
examples.en: That pitcher is right-handed but also writes with his left hand.

examples.ko: 마지막 이닝에 우완 불펜이 마운드에 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A right-handed reliever came up to the mound in the last inning.

explain: 주로 야구에서 '우완 투수'처럼 오른팔로 던지는 투수를 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '좌완'이에요. 일상에서 오른팔을 말할 때는 '오른팔'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used mainly in baseball, as in '우완 투수' for a pitcher who throws with the right arm. The opposite is '좌완'. In daily life, the right arm is just '오른팔'.

en: run about in confusion; run pell-mell

examples.en: At the sudden blackout, the staff ran about in confusion in the lobby.

examples.ko: 지침이 없으니 현장 대응이 우왕좌왕할 수밖에 없지요.
examples.en: With no guidelines, the response on site can't help but be chaotic.

examples.ko: 건물에 불이 나자 사람들이 출구를 찾지 못해 우왕좌왕하며 헤맸어요.
examples.en: When the building caught fire, people couldn't find the exit and wandered around in confusion.

examples.ko: 시험 시간이 부족해서 우왕좌왕하다가 답을 못 썼어요.
examples.en: I ran out of time on the test, flustered, and couldn't write my answers.
Don't panic; calmly do it in order.

examples.ko: 정책이 자꾸 바뀌어서 학교도 우왕좌왕하고 있어요.
examples.en: Policies keep changing, so the schools are also in confusion.

explain: 사람이나 조직이 혼란스러워서 방향을 못 잡을 때 써요. '허둥지둥'은 급해서 서두르는 느낌이고, '우왕좌왕'은 갈피를 못 잡고 이리저리 움직이는 느낌이에요. '갈팡질팡'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It is used when people or organizations are confused and can't find a direction. '허둥지둥' feels like rushing in a hurry, while '우왕좌왕' feels like moving this way and that without direction. '갈팡질팡' is used similarly.

examples.ko: 이 논문은 새 치료법의 우월성을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This paper shows the superiority of the new treatment.

examples.ko: 그는 자기 문화의 우월성만 주장해서 대화가 안 돼요.
examples.en: He only insists on the superiority of his own culture, so we can't talk.

examples.ko: 두 제품 중 어느 쪽의 우월성이 더 큰지 비교해 봤어요.
examples.en: I compared which of the two products has greater superiority.
If you are obsessed with superiority, it is hard to get close to people.
Regardless of technical superiority, the price matters.
He judges people by the superiority of their education.

explain: 논문, 기사, 사회 문제 이야기에서 '우월성을 주장하다', '우월성을 보이다'처럼 써요. '우월감'은 내가 더 낫다고 느끼는 마음이고, '우월성'은 더 낫다는 성질이나 주장을 말해서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is used in papers, articles and social issues, as in '우월성을 주장하다' or '우월성을 보이다'. '우월감' is the inner feeling of being better, while '우월성' refers to the quality or claim of being superior.

examples.en: The child crunches away on a cucumber.

examples.ko: 형이 과자를 우적우적 먹으면서 영화를 봐요.
examples.en: My brother watches a movie while munching on snacks.
The horse is chomping on grass.
I was so hungry that I wolfed down the bread.
If you crunch ice, your teeth hurt.
He took a big crunchy bite of the apple.

explain: 단단하거나 질긴 것을 거칠게 씹는 소리와 모양에 써요. '아삭아삭'은 신선한 채소나 과일의 가벼운 식감이고, '우물우물'은 입 안에서 천천히 씹는 모양이라 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It describes the sound and look of chewing hard or tough food roughly. '아삭아삭' is the light crispness of fresh vegetables or fruit, and '우물우물' is slow chewing in the mouth, so they differ.

examples.en: Every morning birds sing in the trees.
I woke up to the sound of birds chirping.

examples.ko: 숲 속에서 새들이 즐겁게 우짖고 있어요.
examples.en: Birds are chirping happily in the forest.
The bird that had been chirping since dawn has gone quiet.

examples.ko: 참새 한 마리가 베란다에서 우짖다가 날아갔어요.
examples.en: A sparrow chirped on the balcony and then flew away.

examples.ko: 새들이 우짖으면 봄이 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: When birds chirp, it feels like spring has come.

explain: 새가 소리 내는 것에 쓰는 글말 느낌의 표현이라 시나 글에서 자주 나와요. 일상 말로는 '새가 울다'라고 하고, 작은 새가 가볍게 소리 내는 것은 '지저귀다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a somewhat literary word for birds making sounds, common in poems and writing. In daily speech people say '새가 울다', and '지저귀다' is used for small birds chirping lightly.

examples.en: The wall is bumpy, so it feels rough to the touch.

examples.ko: 얼음이 녹았다가 다시 얼어서 우툴두툴한 표면이 그리 미끄럽지는 않았어요.
examples.en: The ice melted and refroze, so the bumpy surface wasn't very slippery.
My facial skin became bumpy, so I went to the hospital.
The road is bumpy, so walk carefully.
The cucumber skin is bumpy, but it tastes good.

examples.ko: 이 돌은 표면이 우툴두툴하게 깎여 있어요.
examples.en: This stone has been cut with a rough, bumpy surface.

explain: '울퉁불퉁하다'가 길이나 땅처럼 크게 굴곡진 곳에 어울린다면, '우툴두툴하다'는 피부, 오이 껍질, 벽처럼 작은 돌기가 많은 표면에 더 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '매끈하다'예요.
explain_en: '울퉁불퉁하다' suits roads and ground with big dips and bumps, while '우툴두툴하다' fits surfaces with many small bumps, such as skin, cucumber peel or walls. The opposite is '매끈하다' (smooth).

examples.en: Troubles keep coming to the family, and I am worried.

examples.ko: 올해는 우환 없이 무사히 지나가면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope this year passes safely without any trouble.

examples.ko: 큰 우환을 겪고 나니 가족의 소중함을 알았어요.
examples.en: After going through a big trouble, I learned how precious family is.

examples.ko: 어머니의 병이 집안의 우환으로 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Mother's illness remains a worry for the family.
The household that suffered from troubles has finally become peaceful.

examples.ko: 아이가 시험에 붙어서 오랜 우환은 사라졌어요.
examples.en: The child passed the exam, so the long-standing worry is gone.

explain: 주로 집안의 걱정거리, 특히 가족의 병이나 불행한 일을 말할 때 써요. 어르신들이 '집에 우환이 있다'처럼 많이 말해요. 일반적인 '걱정'보다 무겁고 오래가는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to a family's troubles, especially a relative's illness or misfortune. Older people often say things like '집에 우환이 있다'. It feels heavier and longer-lasting than ordinary '걱정'.

examples.en: The police blocked the road and guided us to a detour.
Because of construction, please use the detour.
There was a detour, so I wasn't very late.
If this road is blocked, where is the detour?
If you follow the detour signs, you'll reach the main road.
There were many cars on the detour too, so I waited a long time.

explain: 길이 막히거나 공사 중일 때 돌아가는 길이에요. 크게 돌아가는 길이라 빨리 가는 '지름길'과 반대 느낌이고, 좁은 작은 길은 '샛길'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the way you take around a blocked or closed road. Since it is a longer way round, it feels opposite to a '지름길' (shortcut), and a small side path is called a '샛길'.
